I’ll review the completed verification evidence, retire only the baseline entries supported by the lock-contention proof, and run the required checks before closing this phase. I’m using the SASE memory, repository, artifact, and finalization workflows to keep the evidence auditable.


The core checkout and installed extension both match the fixed revision, and the caller changes preserve explicit deadlines. I’m checking the per-test results now; the diagnostic driver’s exit code alone doesn’t establish that its tests passed.


The affected files passed all 272 tests. The controlled lock test reproduced the SQLite error in three baseline nodes on the old core; all three passed on the fixed core, so I’ll retire those entries. The loaded run also caught one process-exit assertion failure in a group-kill test. I’ll retain that entry and the five others whose connection to this fix remains unproven.


The latency review found a real gap: a 25 ms write budget can take about 50 ms because WAL setup restarts its timer after the first busy wait. I’ll correct that narrow core path and verify it before closing the phase. The flake gate also reports 41 exceedances outside the three retired nodes; I’ll record those separately.


The flake gate reports the same 41 exceedances with the original and updated baselines; none is one of the three retired nodes. I’ve recorded the group-kill failure and the attribution limits for the land agent. The main check is still running, and the timer correction is ready for core verification and a rebuild.


The running check detected the core edit and started rebuilding the local Rust extension. I’ll let that run finish. The follow-up verification will show that the new regression test fails with the timer reset, passes with the correction, and keeps the application contention tests passing.


The slow step is the Rust rebuild inside the check. The evidence report now records the exact test counts and the baseline entries being retained. The timer regression uses an established lock and enough scheduling margin to detect the old double wait without relying on a startup race.


The rebuild is still compiling the Python binding. The compiler is active; there’s no new test result yet.


The verification batch is ready. It will preserve the earlier measurements, save the corrected source before testing the old behavior, and record each check’s result separately so the next review can identify any remaining failure.


The corrected Python extension has built, and I’ve run the bounded-lock probes against it while setup builds the matching language server. Those measurements are being saved for audited review; the core regression and final checks still remain.


The corrected build’s bounded-lock probes confirm the timer fix: a 25 ms write budget now tops out at 25.46 ms, down from 49.95 ms. All 30 releasable-lock operations succeeded, and all 20 deliberately blocked operations returned bounded errors with no duplicate records or quarantine.


The rebuild has finished and the lint gates have resumed. The measured deadline correction is working; I’m waiting for this check to settle before handing the remaining verification to a monitor.


All lint and validation stages passed. The check is now running its scoped test selection. The retained baseline entries and proposed follow-ups are documented; closure still depends on the remaining verification.


The normal check expanded to the broad test lane and obtained 11 workers. That adds runtime beyond the focused tests; it is still the required `check` command.


The broad test run is at 37%. I’ll review the failure details when it finishes before deciding whether anything else needs fixing.


The test run has reached 44%. The three baseline retirements remain supported by controlled evidence; the other six entries remain active.


The check is past halfway, at 56%. Its lint and validation stages are green; the test verdict is still pending.


The test run has reached 71%. I’ll keep any failures in the evidence and distinguish new failures from those with an independent existing witness.


The test run is at 87%. The corrected deadline probe has passed; the broad check’s final verdict and the dedicated Rust regression are still outstanding.


The test run is at 94%. Once it settles, I’ll hand the dedicated core regression and repeated contention checks to the prepared monitor.


The test run has reached 99%; the remaining tests and teardown are still running. I’ll wait for the exit status before starting the monitor.


The check finished with 58,227 passing tests and three failures: two completion snapshots and the TUI import-time budget. None is a ToolRun contention failure. I’ll check those three on the unchanged tree and clean base before attributing them, then start the core verification monitor.


All three failures reproduced with identical messages on the clean base using the old core extension. The import guard failure is a module-count cap, not elapsed time. I’ve restored the integration changes exactly and will record these existing failures, then hand the remaining verification to the monitor.


I’m starting the SASE monitor for the core regression’s fail/pass check, both repository checks, and the repeated contention tests. The continuation has the evidence and exact remaining steps. This phase will stay open until those results are reviewed.
